paragraphs: So it is cited in Yalkut, Beshalach, remez 243, but the Mekhilta, Beshalach, Massekhta deShirah, chapter 2, reads Issi ben Shammai.[^1]

notes.text: The whole selected Yalkut Torah 243 paragraph fully names Rabbi Issi ben Azzai; the whole Beeri 2019 Mekhilta Tractate Shirah chapter 2 paragraph names Issi ben Shammai. These positively support Hyman’s two differing forms without merging them. The comparison uses the named Mekhilta section; it does not establish equivalence between differing reference systems.
